subject: Phased onramp & pricing hurdles — MAP milestones tied to SLA concessions
messages:

Subject: Phased onramp & pricing hurdles — MAP milestones tied to SLA concessions

Hi Liam / Kara,

Appreciate the time on the demo last week. Per our conversation I attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP_Initio_v1.pdf) that sequences the evaluation gates and the commercial milestones we'll link to pricing/commit discounts and SLA concessions. Key points up front:

- Goal: get Initio to production traffic (internal pilot -> prod ramp) over a 12 week onramp with a phased discount ladder tied to committed QPS and latency SLOs.
- Commercial construct: graded discounts starting at 10% at initial commit, scaling to 25% when committed throughput and latency targets are met across two consecutive weeks.
- SLA tradeoff: where you commit predictable monthly throughput, Redwood can offer tighter p95 latency targets and smaller incident credit exposure.

Please find highlights in the attached MAP and a brief SLA appendix (SLA_Rollout_Appendix.docx). I'm copying Monica (Solutions) and Neha (Legal/commercial) to keep this lean on our side.

Requested next steps:
1) Review the MAP and the proposed acceptance gates by Nov 5.
2) Confirm a procurement POC for signature and initial purchase order.
3) If acceptable, we’ll finalize DocuSign link for the signature and schedule a kickoff.

I called out an initial commit band (100k tokens/month equivalent) — we can adjust the banding if you prefer different ramp percentages.

Best,
Marcus

Subject: Re: Phased onramp & pricing hurdles — MAP milestones tied to SLA concessions

Thanks Marcus — quick read through. I like the structure but flagged a few concerns for Kara and procurement:

- Our product team is nervous about hard p95 cliffs for discounts. We prefer a ramping SLO (e.g., 200ms -> 150ms -> 120ms) tied to ramp percent rather than absolute immediate targets.
- Credits: can we cap monthly service credits at 15% instead of the unlimited modification currently in the appendix?
- We also need a clear acceptance gate for our security review to be completed before the second discount tier is triggered.

Kara / procurement — are you available for a 20-minute call to walk through the MAP tomorrow?

Regards,
Liam
VP Product, Initio HealthTech
liam.oconnor@initio.ai

Marcus — quick take:
- Agree with Liam’s preference for a stepped SLO ramp rather than immediate p95 cliffs. Propose: Tier A (pilot): p95 <= 200ms; Tier B (scale): p95 <= 160ms; Tier C (prod target): p95 <= 130ms. Each tier must be met for two consecutive weeks to unlock next discount.
- Credits cap: 15% monthly cap is reasonable. For enterprise, we can add an escalation clause for repeated misses.
- Security gate: require security sign-off and evidence (pen-test summary or SOC2 page) before Tier B discount becomes active.

I can draft a short wording for the SLA appendix if you want me to send over now.

-Monica
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@initio.ai>, Kara Jennings <kjennings@initio.ai>

Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2027 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Phased onramp & pricing hurdles — MAP milestones tied to SLA concessions

Liam / Kara,

Thanks — attached is an updated MAP and a concrete table below that reflects Monica’s suggestion and our commercial proposal. If that looks good we’ll roll the language into the DocuSign and push to legal for quick redlines.

Proposed MAP milestones (summary):
- Week 0 (Kickoff): PO signed, onboarding workspace provisioned. Initial discount: 10% applied at billing start.
- Weeks 1–4 (Pilot / Tier A): goal p95 <= 200ms. Commitment: 100k tokens/mo. Unlock: after two consecutive weeks meeting p95 target, Tier B unlocks.
- Weeks 5–8 (Scale / Tier B): goal p95 <= 160ms. Commitment increases to 300k tokens/mo. Unlock: after two consecutive weeks meeting p95 and security gate complete, Tier C unlocks. Discount at Tier B: 15%.
- Weeks 9–12 (Prod / Tier C): goal p95 <= 130ms. Commitment: 1.0M tokens/mo. Discount at Tier C: 25%.

SLA / Credits:
- Monthly service credit cap: 15% of monthly bill.
- Credit triggers: single-week p95 miss >20% of target (measured on Redwood Console on agreed route) -> remedial plan + credits per appendix.
- Repeated misses (>=3 months) escalate to business review with potential termination rights after cure period.

Security gate:
- Security sign-off (email from Initio security POC or SOC2 evidence) required before Tier B discounts can apply. Procurement may withhold Tier B invoices until evidence is shared.

Commercial mechanics:
- Discounts are reconciled monthly on actual committed volume; overage rates apply if actual exceeds committed band.
- DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123 (Initio SIG_v2 prepared)

Attachments: MAP_Initio_v1.pdf (updated), SLA_Rollout_Appendix.docx (updated).

If you’re good, I’ll engage Neha to create the redline-friendly SIG and send the DocuSign. Can we confirm signature by Nov 8 to keep the Nov 15 pilot start?

Best,
Marcus
